objective.stem: A farmer is a person who ___
objective.answer: grows crops or keeps animals for food
distractors: drives a big bus to the town
mends our shoes at the roadside

objective.stem: The farmer who keeps birds for eggs and meat is a ___
Work that begins a new farm, before any seed is planted, is ___
After planting, the farmer removes the ___
The last work in growing a crop, before the money comes, is ___
A fish farmer feeds his fish at set times and keeps the ___
Why does a farmer begin his work very early in the morning?
objective.answer: because the body is cooler and weeds are soft
distractors: because the market is shut down later
because the sun is brighter at noon
because the tools are heavier in rain

objective.stem: A farm visit is when the class goes to the farm to ___
objective.answer: see with the eyes what the class was told
distractors: buy plenty of food for the house
have a long sleep on the grass
play football with the bigger boys

objective.stem: Before we start a farm visit we should ___
objective.answer: shut our shoes and fill the water flask
distractors: leave our books on the ground
carry our lunch in an open bag

objective.stem: On the farm we must not ___
objective.answer: pick the fruit or chase the birds away
distractors: look at the plants in the rows
ask the farmer any good question
wash our hands when we come back

objective.stem: An animal that sits apart from the others in the house is probably ___
A good question to ask the farmer on a visit is ___
objective.answer: when did you plant this crop?

objective.stem: A farm tool is a thing we use to ___
The tool with a broad blade used for tilling and making ridges is the ___
A cutlass is used mainly for ___
objective.answer: clearing the grass and small sticks
distractors: carrying the harvest to the market
sowing the small seeds in rows

objective.stem: A tool with teeth for gathering leaves and leveling a seedbed is the ___
A watering can has a spout with small holes called a ___
The tool with a flat stiff blade that is pushed with the foot into the ground is the ___
Which tool is better for lifting and moving loose sand?
A wheelbarrow carries a big load because it has a ___
objective.answer: wheel, a tray and two handles
distractors: very long rope for pulling it
net and a heavy wooden lid

objective.stem: In loading a barrow, the heavy things are put ___
objective.answer: near the wheel and over it
distractors: at the back by the handles

objective.stem: A wheelbarrow must never be used for carrying ___
A woven carrier used for the harvest and put on the head is a ___
Before we swing a cutlass we must first ___
objective.answer: clear the people and the stones away
distractors: count the leaves on the bush

objective.stem: A tool is kept after work by ___
objective.answer: cleaning off the mud, drying and hanging it
distractors: leaving it there on the wet ground
burying it deep in the planting bed
pouring cold water on the blade

objective.stem: The tool used to fan chaff from grain is the ___
A knapsack sprayer differs from a watering can because it sends a ___
objective.answer: fine mist of medicine on to the leaf
distractors: big stream of water on the root

objective.stem: A sickle is a curved one-hand blade used for ___
The farmers' saying about the two tools that look alike is: a spade digs, a shovel ___
Tools must not be left where a child can step on them, so they are ___
objective.answer: racked or hung with the edge covered
distractors: stood up out in the hot sun

subobjective.stem: Name the four kinds of farmer we learnt and what each keeps or grows.
Mention five works of a crop farmer in order.
Name four things to look for on a crop farm during a visit.
Draw and name the parts of a tool: the working metal and the part in the hand.
Mention the parts of a watering can.
Name four tools used for carrying on the farm.
Sort these into digging and clearing: hoe, cutlass, spade, rake.
Mention the parts of a wheelbarrow.
Name two pairs of tools that look alike and the one difference in each.
Give four rules for storing farm tools well.

theory.stem: Who is a farmer? Explain the work of any two kinds of farmer.
Write on a farm visit: the rules we keep and four things we look for.
Name four farm tools and say what each is used for.
Explain the difference between a spade and a shovel, and between a hoe and a rake.
Write on the care and storage of farm tools.
